intro.title: Discover Erasmusbrug
intro.description:
Erasmusbrug is an iconic bascule bridge located in Rotterdam, Netherlands. This bridge is renowned for its unique architecture and is one of the most recognizable symbols of Rotterdam.

The bridge spans the Nieuwe Maas and connects the north and south of the city. With its imposing white pylon and asymmetrical cable distribution, Erasmusbrug is a masterpiece of modern engineering.

Whether you take a walk across the bridge, admire the sunset from the riverbank, or view the bridge from a sightseeing boat, Erasmusbrug offers you an unforgettable experience. The bridge is also a popular location for events such as the Rotterdam Marathon.

sections.title: Bridge History
sections.content:
Erasmusbrug was designed by the famous architect Ben van Berkel of UNStudio. Construction began in 1986 and the bridge was officially opened in 1996 by Queen Beatrix.

The bridge is named after Desiderius Erasmus, the famous humanist and theologian from the 15th century. With a length of 802 meters and a width of 33 meters, it is an impressive structure that has significantly changed Rotterdam's skyline.

sections.title: Bridge Features
sections.content:
Erasmusbrug features unique characteristics:

• An imposing white pylon 139 meters high
• Asymmetrical cable distribution (single large pylon)
• A bascule (movable section) for shipping traffic
• Two bicycle and pedestrian bridges on either side
• Beautiful lighting at night

These features make Erasmusbrug one of the most photographed locations in Rotterdam.

sections.title: Location
sections.content:
The bridge is strategically located in the center of Rotterdam and spans the Nieuwe Maas. It connects the central station area with Kop van Zuid.

From the bridge, you have a stunning view of Rotterdam's skyline, including the White House, the Euromast, and the Wilhelminapier. The bridge is easily accessible by public transport and is within walking distance from the central station.

sections.title: Events
sections.content:
Erasmusbrug is not only an important traffic artery, but also a popular location for events:

• Rotterdam Marathon - the finish line is on Erasmusbrug
• Rotterdam Harbor Days - special lighting and activities
• Photography and film shoots - frequently used as a film location
• Running events and charity runs

Visit the official Rotterdam website for the most current event schedule.

transport.title: How to Get Here
transport.fromCenterDesc: Walk about 15-20 minutes via the Willemsbrug or take tram 20 to Kop van Zuid. Erasmusbrug is within walking distance from the station.
transport.fromStationDesc: Take train to Rotterdam Central from The Hague, Amsterdam etc, then walk or take tram.
transport.fromAirportDesc: Take the bus to Rotterdam Central, then tram 20 or walk 15 minutes to the bridge.
transport.publicTransportDesc: Trams 20, 23 and 25 stop near Erasmusbrug. Metro station Wilhelminaplein is 5 minutes walk away.
transport.walkingDesc: The bridge is excellently accessible on foot or by bike. There are separate bike paths on the bridge.
transport.drivingDesc: Parking in the area is paid. P+R locations offer cheaper options. The bridge itself is not accessible for cars.

route.title: Recommended Visit Route
route.overview: Erasmusbrug is perfect for a half-day or full-day visit. We recommend arriving in the morning for peaceful photos, exploring the surrounding area in the afternoon, and enjoying the illuminated skyline in the evening. Plan about 2-3 hours for the entire visit.
steps: Arrive at Erasmusbrug in the morning, walk across the bridge for stunning views
Visit Kop van Zuid on the south side of the bridge
Take photos of the iconic white pylon from the riverbank
Enjoy lunch at one of the restaurants on the Wilhelminapier
Visit Rotterdam's harbor area and learn about maritime history
Walk back across the bridge during golden hour for the best photos
Admire the bridge lighting in the evening
End your day with a drink at one of the rooftop bars in the center

items.name: Zhang Ming
items.text: Erasmusbrug was the highlight of our Rotterdam trip! The bridge architecture is incredible, and the white pylon is so impressive. The skyline views from the bridge were breathtaking - absolutely worth a visit!

items.name: Li Meiling
items.text: Walking across the bridge was an amazing experience. You can see 360-degree views of Rotterdam. The evening light show was particularly beautiful - we took so many photos!

items.name: Wang Jianguo
items.text: The architectural design of this bridge is stunning. The asymmetrical cable distribution is so unique. Great location, very close to Central Station - super convenient transportation.

items.name: Chen Xiaowen
items.text: Among all the landmarks in Rotterdam, Erasmusbrug is definitely top 3. Very peaceful in the early morning, perfect for photography. The night light show is also a must-see!

officialManagement.title: About Erasmusbrug
officialManagement.text:
Erasmusbrug is an iconic bascule bridge located in Rotterdam, Netherlands. The bridge was designed by Ben van Berkel and opened in 1996.

This bridge features unique architecture with an imposing white pylon 139 meters high. It is one of the most recognizable symbols of Rotterdam and a popular tourist attraction.
